plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: In the cold of midwinter, glossy evergreen shrubs open rose-like blooms with a boss of golden stamens at the center. The flowers stand out against dark, leathery leaves in woodlands and temple gardens, and they are among the most welcome sights of the season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Wild plants flower from January to March, so early January is the start of the season.
plants.location: Japan, in coastal woodlands and gardens across the warmer parts of the country
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. In Japan the camellia has long been linked with winter and with the arrival of the new year.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Small, nodding white flowers push up through frosty soil, each with three outer petals and a green-marked inner cup. They form drifts in woodlands, churchyards and old gardens. For many people they are the first sign that spring is on its way.
plants.bloomingSeason: Starts blooming in January and continues through March
plants.location: Woodlands, churchyards and gardens across the United Kingdom and Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make a natural antifreeze-like compound that helps them push through frozen ground. They also contain galantamine, a compound that has been developed into a medicine used for Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Hippeastrum hybrids
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems carry huge trumpet-shaped blooms, often four or more on one stem. They bring bold color to winter windowsills. The flowers open a few weeks after the bulb is planted, which is why they are a favorite for brightening the darkest months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late fall through mid-winter, roughly November to February
plants.location: Indoors in homes and conservatories across the Northern Hemisphere, descended from South American species
plants.funFact: Amaryllis bulbs hold enough stored energy to bloom with no soil at all. A bulb set on a bed of pebbles over water can flower, and the stem can grow several inches in a single day.
